title: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with PyTorch Geometric (PYTH_185_S1 to PYTH_185_S8)

slides.title: Graph Representation Learning
slides.prompt: Graph Neural Networks operate on graph-structured data (nodes, edges, and features) using message passing algorithms.
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch
from torch_geometric.data import Data

edge_index = torch.tensor([[0, 1, 1, 2], [1, 0, 2, 1]], dtype=torch.long)
x = torch.tensor([[-1], [0], [1]], dtype=torch.float)
data = Data(x=x, edge_index=edge_index)

slides.title: Edge Index Format in PyTorch Geometric
slides.prompt: Fill in the PyG Data attribute used to store graph connectivity in COO sparse format `[2, num_edges]`.

slides.title: Message Passing Mechanism
slides.prompt: How do Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) update a node's hidden feature representation?
options: By aggregating feature messages from immediate target neighbor nodes followed by non-linear transformation
By flattening graph topology into standard 1D linear sequences
By running recurrent sequence models over node creation timestamps
slides.correctAnswer: By aggregating feature messages from immediate target neighbor nodes followed by non-linear transformation

slides.title: Graph-Level Pooling (Global Readout)
slides.prompt: Which operation summarizes all individual node representations into a single graph-level feature vector for classification?

slides.title: Graph Attention Networks (GAT)
slides.prompt: Fill in the GNN layer type that assigns anisotropic attention weights to neighboring nodes during message passing.
slides.codeSnippet:
from torch_geometric.nn import ___
conv = GATConv(in_dim, out_dim, heads=4)

slides.title: Oversmoothing Problem in Deep GNNs
slides.prompt: What occurs when stacking too many message-passing graph layers (e.g., > 10 layers)?
options: Node representations converge to identical vectors, losing localized structural information (Oversmoothing)
The model memory consumption drops to zero
Node feature values overflow to infinity
slides.correctAnswer: Node representations converge to identical vectors, losing localized structural information (Oversmoothing)
